citation: Ubachukwu, Mork, Benz and Schäfer (2024), ALICE2Modelica, Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.14827922
description: ALICE2Modelica is a toolchain that generates Modelica building models automatically for building control and simulation. It was developed at Forschungszentrum Jülich by Eziama Ubachukwu, Maximilian Mork, Jakob Benz and Jonas Schäfer and published on Zenodo on 14 June 2024. It builds on ALICE, a small language that describes the geometry of room envelopes: from ALICE files, SVG floor plans and parametrisable Modelica room templates, Python scripts generate Modelica room and whole-building models including heating, ventilation and air-conditioning systems, so large buildings can be modelled without hand-coding each room. Coverage: any building for which floor plans and ALICE descriptions exist; the archive ships room templates with and without floor heating and coupled variants. Access: a zip archive of the repository on Zenodo, whose file listing shows Python scripts and Modelica templates. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free, though a Modelica simulation environment is needed to run the generated models. Caveats: a research toolchain with a single release and limited documentation outside the archive. Simulation uses are room-level building models for control design, model predictive control and building digital twins. Related records: the Modelica Buildings Library and the IBPSA Modelica library.
